heading: Demystifying ERP: The Backbone of Modern Business Operations
cardTitle: Demystifying ERP: The Backbone of Modern Business Operations
excerpt: In today's dynamic business landscape, ERP, which stands for Enterprise Resource Planning, plays a pivotal role in the integrated management of core business processes. While this term might sound complex, let's delve into a practical understanding of what ERP is and why it's essential for businesses of all sizes.
html:
Introduction:

In today's dynamic business landscape, ERP, which stands for Enterprise Resource Planning, plays a pivotal role in the integrated management of core business processes. While this term might sound complex, let's delve into a practical understanding of what ERP is and why it's essential for businesses of all sizes.

Understanding ERP:

Let’s understand the need of ERP by taking example of one of the most important business processes – sales. For any organization, sales is the lifeblood; it’s the very reason why a company exists in first place. While sales may seem like a straightforward process, it encompasses eight intricate steps! Yes, you read that right – sales is an 8-step process!

Step 1 – Marketing:

In simple words, marketing is all about informing potential customers about products or services. This entails planning numerous marketing campaigns and may require specialized software to manage these activities. One of the outcomes of this process is ideally to generate the leads.

Step 2 – Customer Relationship Management (CRM):

Converting potential leads into paying customers necessitates consistent follow-ups and relationship management. Customer Relationship Management (CRM) software is a vital tool in this endeavor.

Step 3 – Order Management:

Once customer interest is piqued & it gets converted, efficient management of incoming orders is critical in order to create a good first impression on such newly converted customers. After all, you don’t want to miss on an order, do you? This is where Order Management software steps in to streamline this process.

Step 4 – Transportation Management:

Especially for businesses dealing in physical goods, optimizing warehouse space, transportation routes, inventory, and transportation costs is paramount – to an extent that this can make or break the business. Transportation Management software helps optimize these crucial aspects by controlling the cost and enhancing the execution quality.

Step 5 – Billing:

Invoicing customers for products or services sold is a key aspect from overall bookkeeping or accounting perspective. Billing software simplifies this process, making it more efficient at scale.

Step 6 – Collection:

In larger organizations, a significant portion of sales transactions occurs on credit. So, recovering the cash from such customers to whom you have sold on credit requires continuous follow-ups. This is precisely the step, which collection software streamlines.

Step 7 – Cash Management:

In today's diverse payment landscape, efficient management of cash inflows from various sources is crucial. It plays an important role from working capital management perspective. Sophisticated Cash Management software helps manage the cash effectively & also helps reconcile the inflows effectively – at scale.

Step 8 – After Sales:

Providing exemplary after-sales service is vital to cultivate long-term customer relationships. This phase focuses on turning one-time buyers into repeat customers.

The Significance of ERP:

So, the point is – one seemingly straightforward business process such as sales, comprises as many as 8 different steps. And in a typical large business, it needs to handle a multitude of other such processes, including Purchasing, Payables, Asset Management, Human Resources, and many more. All these processes can be further bifurcated in various sub-steps as we did for Sales. Now just imagine that – if the business has to use different software for each step of each such business process, how much chaos it will lead to – since these software solutions are not going to communicate with each other seamlessly. Thus, such disintegrated software landscape is more likely to cause more problems than to provide solutions to the original problem statements that they set out to resolve!

Enters the “ERP software” which is a SINGLE UNIFORM SOFTWARE that integrates all these processes & steps into a comprehensive solution, eliminating the need for multiple disparate software tools. Hope you got the point as to why ERP software is needed in any large business!

Conclusion:

Traditionally, ERP software implementation used to be a mammoth task involving multi-million-dollar budgets & multi-year timelines just to commence the use of such software! However, in today's digital age, ERP solutions have become more accessible and cost-effective, even for small and medium-sized enterprises. All thanks to SaaS – we will learn more about it in our next blogs!

title: How Managers Can Approve Time Cards in Oracle Cloud | Step-by-Step Guide
description: Learn how managers can review and approve time cards in Oracle Cloud. A step-by-step guide to ensure accurate time tracking and payroll processing.
heading: How Managers Can Approve Time Cards in Oracle Cloud
cardTitle: How Managers Can Approve Time Cards in Oracle Cloud
excerpt: How Managers Can Approve Time Cards in Oracle Cloud | Step-by-Step Guide
html:
Introduction

Approving time cards is a crucial responsibility for managers to ensure accurate payroll processing and compliance. This guide provides a step-by-step process for managers to efficiently review and approve time cards in Oracle Cloud.

This Blog will walk you through the steps for managers to approve time cards, providing clear and detailed instructions to ensure a smooth approval process.

Navigate to the Time Management sub-menu available under the My Client Group menu on the Oracle home page.

Click on the Team Time Cards section from left-hand side.

Search for your team's time cards using parameters such as Person Name, Person Number, From Date, To Date, or Status.

Enter the required values in the search parameters and click on Search.

Oracle Cloud will display the results based on the values entered in the search parameters.

There are two options to approve a time card. The first option is to select the relevant time card and click on the Approve button from the Actions drop-down menu.

The second option is to select the relevant time card and click on the Approve button directly to approve it.

Once approved, Oracle Cloud will display a confirmation message. Click on Close and then return to the Oracle home page to complete the process.

Thank You.

title: How to Review, Update, and Approve Time Cards in Oracle Cloud | Step-by-Step Guide
description: Learn how to review, update, and approve time cards in Oracle Cloud. A step-by-step guide for HR and payroll professionals.
heading: How to Review, Update, and Approve Time Cards in Oracle Cloud
cardTitle: How to Review, Update, and Approve Time Cards in Oracle Cloud
excerpt: How to Review, Update, and Approve Time Cards in Oracle Cloud | Step-by-Step Guide
html:
Introduction

Efficient time card management in Oracle Cloud ensures accurate payroll processing and workforce tracking. This guide walks you through the process of reviewing, updating, and approving time cards for your team, ensuring a smooth approval process.

Blog for reviewing, updating, and approving time cards, providing clear and detailed instructions to ensure a smooth approval process.

Navigate to the Time Management sub-menu available under the My Client Group menu on the Oracle home page.

Click on the Team Time Cards section.

Search for your team’s time cards using various parameters such as Person Name, Person Number, From Date, To Date, and Status.

Enter the search criteria, such as the period or status (For Example Entered, Saved, Submitted), and click on Search.

Oracle Cloud displays the results based on the values provided in the search parameters. Select the relevant time card and click on Edit and Approve.

Enter the number of hours the person worked for the projects and tasks on the corresponding days and dates, then click on Save.

Oracle Cloud displays a confirmation message. Click on OK to proceed.

Once the team time card is edited and updated, click on Next to proceed.

Click on the Submit button to submit the time card for approval.

Oracle Cloud displays a confirmation message. Click on OK to proceed.

Alternatively, as the line manager, you can directly click on the Submit and Approve button to approve the time card.

Oracle Cloud displays a confirmation message. Click on OK to complete the process.

Thank You.

title: How to Create a Capital Project from a Template in Oracle Cloud | Step-by-Step Guide
description: Learn how to efficiently set up a capital project using a project template in Oracle Cloud. A detailed step-by-step guide for project managers and ERP professionals.
heading: How to Create a Capital Project from a Template in Oracle Cloud
cardTitle: How to Create a Capital Project from a Template in Oracle Cloud
excerpt: How to Create a Capital Project from a Template in Oracle Cloud | Step-by-Step Guide
html:
Introduction

Creating a capital project in Oracle Cloud using a predefined project template simplifies the setup process and ensures consistency. This guide provides a step-by-step approach to help project managers create a capital project efficiently within the Oracle ERP system.

Follow the precise instructions below to efficiently set up the capital project from the capital project template.

Click the Projects menu and then select the Project Financial Management sub-menu.

On the 'My Projects' screen, click the Plus icon to create a project using the project template.

Click the drop-down in the Source Template field, and search for the relevant capital project template. Please note that only templates you have access to will be displayed.

Select the required capital project template from the list, and additional fields will automatically populate in the Create Project window based on your project template selection.

Enter the capital project name and number, ensuring both are unique.

By default, Oracle Cloud sets the current system date as the project start date, but you can click the Calendar icon to change it if needed.

Click the Calendar icon to select the project end date, noting that this date is tentative and can be updated later if needed.

The Organization and Legal Entity values defaulted from the selected project template.

Click the Search button to select the Project Manager for the project.

Search for the Project Manager using options like Name or Email, then click Search.

Once the desired search result appears, select the relevant row and click OK to assign the person as the Project Manager.

Once all details are entered, click Save and Continue to create the project in the Oracle Cloud.

After creating the capital project, you will be redirected to the Manage Financial Project Plan screen. Details on updating the Financial Project Plan are covered in the subsequent process manuals.

Click Save and Close to complete the process.

title: How to Locate, Review, and Delete Time Cards in Oracle Cloud | Step-by-Step Guide
description: Learn how to locate, review, and delete time cards in Oracle Cloud. A step-by-step guide for HR and payroll professionals.

excerpt: How to Locate, Review, and Delete Time Cards in Oracle Cloud | Step-by-Step Guide
html:
Introduction

Managing time cards effectively in Oracle Cloud is essential for accurate payroll processing and time tracking. This guide provides a step-by-step approach to locating, reviewing, and deleting time cards within Oracle ERP, ensuring a smooth and error-free process.

In this blog, we will walk you through the necessary steps to locate, review, and delete time cards, ensuring that you can handle the process smoothly and accurately.

Navigate to the Time Management sub-menu available under the My Client Group menu on the Oracle home page.

Click on the Team Time Cards section.

You can search for your team’s time cards using various parameters such as Person Name, Person Number, From Date, To Date, and Status.

Enter the required values in the search parameters and click on Search.

Oracle Cloud will display the results based on the search parameters provided. Select the relevant time card you wish to delete.

There are two options to delete a time card. The first option is to select the relevant time card and click on the Delete button from the Actions drop-down menu.

The second option is to select the relevant time card and click on the cross button to delete the time card.

Oracle Cloud will display a warning message. Click on Yes to proceed.

Once the time card is deleted, Oracle Cloud will display a confirmation message. Click on Close and then the Home button to complete the process.

Thank you

title: How to Review and Submit Project Hours in Oracle Cloud | Step-by-Step Guide

heading: How to Review and Submit Project Hours in Oracle Cloud

excerpt: How to Review and Submit Project Hours in Oracle Cloud | Step-by-Step Guide
html:
Introduction

Reviewing and submitting project hours is essential for accurate payroll and project tracking. This guide walks you through the process of managing time cards in Oracle Cloud efficiently.

This blog will take you through the steps to review and submit your project hours, offering clear and detailed instructions for a seamless process.

Navigate to the 'Time and Absences' sub-menu under the 'Me' menu on the Oracle Home page.

Click on the 'Existing Time Cards' section.

Select the 'Time Period' option and You can search the existing time cards with parameters such as From Date and To Date.

Select the timecard period you want to edit, review, or submit, and then click 'Search.'

Oracle Cloud will display results based on the values entered in the search parameters. Click on the hyperlink for the period start date of the timecard you wish to edit, review, or submit.

Select the projects and tasks, then enter or edit the hours worked for each project and task on the respective days and dates. Review the time entries and click 'Save.'

Click the 'Submit' button to submit the timecard entry for approval and complete the process.

The timecard status will update to 'Submitted.' Click on 'Home' to finish the process.

Thank You.

title: Step-by-Step Guide to Asset Mass Addition and Posting in Oracle Cloud
description: Learn how to efficiently conduct asset mass addition and post to fixed assets in Oracle Cloud. Follow this guide for a smooth capitalization process.
heading: Conducting Asset Mass Addition and Posting to Fixed Assets in Oracle Cloud
cardTitle: How to Record Project Hours in Oracle Cloud
excerpt: How to Record Project Hours in Oracle Cloud | Step-by-Step Guide
html:
Introduction

This guide provides a detailed step-by-step process for conducting asset mass addition and posting to fixed assets in Oracle Cloud. Follow these steps to ensure accurate capitalization and accounting of assets.

Blog shows process of conducting Asset Mass Addition and posting to Fixed Assets in the Oracle Cloud. These steps will help you navigate through the necessary actions efficiently.

Click on the 'Assets' sub-menu under the 'Fixed Assets' menu from the Oracle Home page.

Transferred assets will appear in the 'Incomplete' section if any mandatory details, such as location or category, are missing. If all mandatory details are filled at the project level, the assets will appear in the 'Ready to Post'

Click on the 'Ready to Post' section to view all the assets that are ready for capitalization. Select the asset line you want to capitalize within the Fixed Assets module and initiate the capitalization process by clicking on the 'Post All' button.

A notification will pop up confirming that Oracle has initiated a scheduled process in the background to post Fixed Asset lines for capitalization.

Click on the 'Schedule Processes' sub-menu under the 'Tools' menu to check the process status.

Keep clicking the ‘Refresh’ button until the process status shows as ‘Succeeded.’ Once successful, navigate back to the Oracle Home page.

Navigate to the 'Assets' sub-menu under the 'Fixed Assets' menu from the Oracle Home page.

Run the ‘Create Accounting’ process from the Task list in the Fixed Asset Module to generate accounting entries for asset capitalization.

Enter the values in the provided parameters such as Book, Process Category, End Date and Accounting Mode.

Review all the entered parameter values and click on 'Submit.'

Oracle Cloud will display a confirmation message. Click on 'OK' to proceed. Once successful, navigate back to the Oracle Home page.

Click on the 'Schedule Processes' sub-menu under the 'Tools' menu to check the process status.

Keep clicking the ‘Refresh’ button until the process status shows as ‘Succeeded.’ Once successful, navigate back to the Oracle Home page.

Click on the 'Assets' sub-menu under the 'Fixed Assets' menu from the Oracle Home page.

Select 'Inquire Assets' from the Task list.

Enter the Asset Number or Category in the parameters and click on 'Search.'

Review the capitalized assets to date and scroll down to see further details.

Click on 'Recent Additions' to validate the details of the recently capitalized assets.

Thank You.

title: Step-by-Step Guide to Closing a Project in Oracle Cloud
description: Learn how to efficiently close a project in Oracle Cloud. Follow this detailed guide to ensure a smooth project closure process.
heading: How to Close a Project in Oracle Cloud
cardTitle: How to Review Allocation Costs in Oracle Cloud
excerpt: How to Review Allocation Costs in Oracle Cloud | Step-by-Step Guide
html:
Introduction

Closing a project in Oracle Cloud involves reviewing financial settings, commitments, and exceptions before finalizing the status change. This guide provides step-by-step instructions to ensure a seamless project closure process.

This blog provides detailed instructions on project closure process within the Oracle Cloud.

Navigate to the 'Project Financial Management' sub-menu under the 'Projects' menu from the Oracle home page.

On the ‘My Projects’ page, search for a project by entering the project name or number into the search field.

Select the relevant project row and click on the hyperlink of the project name. Choose 'Manage Financial Project Settings' from the available options.

Click on the 'General' tab on the 'Manage Financial Project Settings' page.

Review the current project status. Before proceeding to close the project, ensure to review key aspects such as project commitments, exceptions, and accounting.

Observe the 'From' and 'To' project status fields. The 'From' status indicates the current project status, while the 'To' status displays the next allowable status based on the project status configuration.

Select the applicable project status in the 'To' project field. If needed, add comments in the 'Comments' section.

Review the change history of the project status. Click on 'Save and Close' to submit the project.

Confirm that the project status has changed from 'Active' to 'Closed'.

Complete the process by clicking on 'Done'.

Thank You.

title: How to Close a Project Period in Oracle Cloud | Step-by-Step Guide

html:
Introduction

Closing a project period in Oracle Cloud is an essential step in financial management. This guide provides clear and detailed instructions on how to efficiently complete the project period closing process.

This blog provides detailed instructions on how to perform a project period closing in Oracle Cloud. Follow the precise steps below to efficiently complete the project period closing process.

Navigate to the 'General Accounting' menu and select the 'Period Close' sub-menu.

Select the period and Project sub-ledger that is currently set to 'Open' or 'Pending' status.

Select the project period with the 'Active' or 'Pending Close' status and click on 'Close Period' to close that period finally.

Oracle Cloud will initiate the process to close the period.

Click on the Refresh button until the period status updates to 'Closed'.

Select the 'Done' option to complete the process.

title: How to Record Project Hours in Oracle Cloud | Step-by-Step Guide
description: Learn how to accurately record your project hours in Oracle Cloud. A step-by-step guide for entering and managing timecards effectively.
heading: How to Record Project Hours in Oracle Cloud
cardTitle: How to Close a Project in Oracle Cloud
excerpt: Step-by-Step Guide to Closing a Project in Oracle Cloud
html:
Introduction

Recording project hours accurately is crucial for payroll processing and project tracking. This guide provides step-by-step instructions on how to enter and manage timecards in Oracle Cloud.

This Blog will walk you through the steps of recording your project hours in Oracle Cloud, providing clear and detailed instructions to ensure a smooth process.

Navigate to the 'Time and Absences' sub-menu under the 'Me' menu on the Oracle Home page.

Click on the 'Add Time Card' section.

Click on the plus button to enter time for the projects and tasks.

Click on the calendar icon, select the required weekday for which you want to enter time, and then click 'OK'.

On the timecard header, you will see personal information such as Name, Number, Position, and Job, along with timecard details like the period.

Scroll down, click the drop-down menu to search for and select the project. Ensure that the project is in active status.

Once the project is selected, click the drop-down menu in the Task field to search for and select the required task. Ensure that the task is marked as chargeable in the 'Financial Project Plan'.

Similarly, click on the 'Expenditure Type' drop-downs and select the relevant details.

Enter the number of hours worked for the projects and tasks on the corresponding days and dates. If needed, you can add multiple projects and tasks within the same timecard period.

After entering the necessary information, click on 'Save'.

Click on 'Save and Close' to save your changes and exit this screen.

The timecard status will update to 'Saved.' Click on 'Home' to finish the process.

Thank You.

title: How to Review Allocation Costs in Oracle Cloud | Step-by-Step Guide
description: Learn how to review and manage allocation costs in Oracle Cloud. A step-by-step guide for project cost tracking and financial management.
heading: How to Review Allocation Costs in Oracle Cloud
cardTitle: Conducting Asset Mass Addition and Posting to Fixed Assets in Oracle Cloud
excerpt: Step-by-Step Guide to Asset Mass Addition and Posting in Oracle Cloud
html:
Introduction

Effectively managing and reviewing allocation costs ensures accurate financial tracking in Oracle Cloud. This guide provides step-by-step instructions on how to search, refine, and review allocation cost transactions within the Project Costs section.

Here we will cover everything from accessing the Project Costs section to using advanced search criteria, helping you efficiently manage and review allocation costs.

From the Oracle home page, click the 'Cost' sub-menu under the Projects menu.

Navigate to 'Manage Project Costs' from the Task list.

Search for the project cost using parameters such as Project Name, Number, Expenditure Organization etc. Refine your search further by using additional criteria like Expenditure Business Unit, Transaction Source, Expenditure Date, Expenditure Type etc. For more parameters, click on the 'Advance' button.

On the Advanced screen, enter the required details in the search parameters to inquire about the allocation cost. For more search options, select the 'Advanced' option. To filter allocation cost transactions, set the Expenditure Type to 'Allocation' and click 'Search.'

A table will appear showing all allocation cost transactions of the selected project.

Review the allocated cost by selecting the cost transaction line you wish to examine. Click on the transaction number hyperlink to view more details.

Navigate to the General tab to view the transaction source document from the allocation expenditure and review the other tabs.

Click 'Done' to complete the process.



Thank You.

title: How to Review Time Card Statuses and Address Exceptions in Oracle Cloud | Step-by-Step Guide
description: Learn how to review time card statuses, identify time exceptions, and resolve worker-specific issues in Oracle Cloud. A step-by-step guide for HR and payroll professionals.
heading: How to Review Time Card Statuses and Address Exceptions in Oracle Cloud
cardTitle: How to Review Time Card Statuses and Address Exceptions in Oracle Cloud
excerpt: How to Review Time Card Statuses and Address Exceptions in Oracle Cloud | Step-by-Step Guide
html:
Introduction

Accurate time tracking is essential for payroll and workforce management. This guide walks you through the process of reviewing time card statuses, identifying exceptions, and resolving errors in Oracle Cloud to ensure a smooth approval process.

This Blog provides clear and detailed instructions on reviewing time card statuses, identifying time exceptions, and addressing other worker-specific exceptions to ensure a smooth and seamless approval process.

Navigate to the Time Management sub-menu available under the My Client Group menu on the Oracle home page.

Click on the Team Management Overview section.

Select the time period to view the details below.

Review the count of time card statuses such as Approved, Entered, Saved, and Submitted.

Click on the hyperlink for the desired status to view the corresponding time card details for the selected period. Repeat the same steps to check other statuses.

View the details of approved time cards for the selected period.

Review the count of Transfer Process Exceptions, including time cards that failed to transfer and incomplete time transfer processes.

Click on the hyperlink in the respective row to view the details.

Review all worker-related exceptions, including Person Name, Time Card Period, Time Exceptions, Time Cards in Errors, Rejected Time Cards, and Transfer Process Errors. Click on the hyperlink in the respective row to view the details.

Thank You.
